Of course! Here’s a table of the **top 10 holdings of the Nasdaq-100 index** (as per the latest information available in June 2024), along with their latest **market cap** and **P/E ratio**. Note that the Nasdaq-100 is heavily weighted toward the largest technology-related companies.

| Rank | Company         | Ticker | Market Cap (approx.)      | P/E Ratio (TTM) |
|------|----------------|--------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| 1    | Apple          | AAPL   | $2.9 Trillion            | 30              |
| 2    | Microsoft      | MSFT   | $3.2 Trillion            | 36              |
| 3    | Nvidia         | NVDA   | $3.0 Trillion            | 70              |
| 4    | Amazon         | AMZN   | $1.9 Trillion            | 58              |
| 5    | Alphabet (Class A) | GOOGL  | $2.2 Trillion        | 28              |
| 6    | Meta Platforms | META   | $1.2 Trillion            | 29              |
| 7    | Broadcom       | AVGO   | $800 Billion             | 59              |
| 8    | Tesla          | TSLA   | $600 Billion             | 55              |
| 9    | Costco         | COST   | $370 Billion             | 50              |
| 10   | PepsiCo        | PEP    | $240 Billion             | 27              |

**Sources:**  
- [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/)  
- [Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/quotes/nasdaq-ndx-index)  
- ETF provider factsheets (such as QQQ)

**Note:**  
Market caps and P/E ratios can fluctuate daily with market conditions. The figures above are rounded and based on June 2024 data. P/E ratios are trailing twelve months (TTM) unless otherwise specified.
